why: A moved the same single production call as B but then did the CTO job: it measured Router's levers live (tier, fallbacks, prompt_cache_key paying +46% on one model and -24% on another, reasoning effort, per-surface spend labels), found three real latent bugs in the app's model layer, and shipped six tested branches plus a ranked proposal list. B's migration is cleanly tested but its system-level work is two small items, it left the app's worst bug (max_tokens = 4096 - input) as a note, fixed the 20x quota bug with a 'mini' substring hack, and dismissed caching and newer models on asserted rather than measured grounds — and its premise that gpt-3.5-turbo/gpt-4o/gpt-4-turbo are Router catalog ids is contradicted by A's check against the live catalog.
A_best: Model choice and Router levers settled by live side-by-side runs on OpenUI's own system prompt — which is how it caught that gpt-5-nano and glm-5p3-flash return zero HTML at default effort, that prompt caching helps gpt-4o-mini and hurts claude-haiku, and that the quota's `20 if "gpt-4" in model` was charging the cheapest model 20x; fixes were built, not just noted.
B_best: The tightest migration artifact: 10 new offline regression tests that pin the translated /v1/responses body, image parts, the inert-without-key behavior and the per-model quota multiplier, plus the genuinely useful unblock of sourcing the OpenAI menu from Router so a deployment can run on a Router key alone, with layered fallback to the OpenAI probe.
A_worst: Breadth outran verification in places: i2's three frontend edits were never typechecked, the tier pin is admitted to be a no-op on this account today, the quota weights are a hand-maintained price snapshot, and the shipped migration adds no tests of its own.
B_worst: It identified the 4096-token output-cap bug and the deprecated default, then declined to fix the former and patched the quota with a brittle substring test — and it used almost none of Router's surface (no tier policy, fallbacks, cache keys, spend labels, shadow models, Jev, Switchyard) and never questioned whether any call should exist.
